provenance: CRC party registers 11a–11d (docs/class-11*.md), compiled Oct 4, 2026; ported from Coalition Builder v2 / Party Map v2.
bioSource: Wikipedia, accessed Oct 2026, via the research memo and party registers.

parties.name: Likud
parties.surplusLine: Surplus: Religious Zionism (agreed Sep 8; reported unsigned Sep 15)

who.text: Founded Sept 13, 1973 by Begin and Sharon; won power in 1977 with 43 seats.
Netanyahu has led it since 2005 (and 1993–99). The Aug 17, 2026 primary put Eli Cohen first; Netanyahu used reserved slots to move hardliners down.
No written 2026 platform; Likud “does not participate in questionnaires.”

voters.text: Its 2022 voters were 57% traditional, 32% secular, 10% national-religious, 1% Haredi. It won 46.5% of traditional voters and 20% of secular voters.
Strong in periphery cities: Beersheba 42%, Eilat 42%, Ashkelon 40% in 2021.
First-time voters (18–22): 14%, behind Yashar's 16%.

draft.text: Netanyahu revived the Haredi exemption bill as the coalition fell apart; Likud's Sharren Haskel vowed to fight it.

courts.text: Levin: “We'll wait for the next term, when two-thirds of the Supreme Court justices' seats become vacant.” Professional members lose their veto under the new judge-selection law.

war.text: Rejected Trump's 15-point plan; no withdrawal “until Hamas is genuinely disarmed.”

wb.text: “As long as I am prime minister, no Palestinian state will arise.” (In July 2025 all Likud ministers urged applying sovereignty.)

names.name: Talik Gvili
names.note: mother of Ran Gvili, the last hostage returned

pledges.text: “A strong right-wing government led by me.”
Petitioned to bar the Joint List; Likud, Shas and UTJ representatives voted to bar the Joint List and Ra'am.

surplusPartner.text: Religious Zionism. Agreed Sept 8; reported still unsigned Sept 15. Final status not found.

quote.text: There is no straight. Yashar is a bluff. There's either left or right… Do you want a Palestinian state? (or) do you want a Jewish state?
quote.speaker: Benjamin Netanyahu

bios.name: Benjamin Netanyahu
bios.text: Born 1949 in Tel Aviv. Prime minister 1996–99, 2009–21 and since 2022, the longest-serving in Israel's history. The first sitting prime minister charged with a crime; his trial began May 24, 2020, and he requested a pardon in November 2025.

who.text: Founded 2012. Israel Policy Forum calls it the “ideological continuation” of Meir Kahane's Kach, which was outlawed in 1994.
Ben-Gvir has led it since 2019. It won 6 seats in 2022 inside the Religious Zionism joint list. He left the government in Jan 2025 over the ceasefire and returned in March 2025.

voters.text: 2022: 6 seats as part of the Religious Zionism joint list (516,470 votes, 10.84%, 14 seats in all).
Draws “traditional Mizrahi voters from the periphery” (Finkelstein).
13% of Haredi first-time voters.
Courting disappointed Likud and Shas voters.

draft.text: Backed the July 14 law banning arrests of draft evaders; proposes Haredi tracks in police and Border Police: “enter service as Haredi and leave it as Haredi.”

courts.text: Backed the 2023 judicial reforms; wants political control of judicial appointments.

war.text: “Disengagement 710” plan: an emigration ministry and 250,000 Gazan departures a year, NIS 10 billion. “This is a free choice; we are not forcing anyone to leave, but there is encouragement.”

wb.text: Opposes a Palestinian state and evacuating settlers. On Temple Mount prayer: Jews “feel that they are the rightful owners of this place.”

pledges.text: A “fully right-wing government”; no unity with centrists, no Arab parties; demands the Defense or Justice ministry; no Palestinian-state talks.

quote.text: We survived Pharaoh, we will survive Keir Starmer as well.
quote.speaker: Itamar Ben-Gvir, on UK sanctions

bios.name: Itamar Ben-Gvir
bios.text: Born 1976 to Iraqi-Jewish parents. Active in Kach's youth movement; convicted in 2007 of incitement and support for a terror organization. National Security Minister from December 2022; left in January 2025 and returned in March 2025.

who.text: Founded 1984 as “Shomrei Sefarad” in protest at Agudat Yisrael's thin Sephardi representation, under Rav Ovadia Yosef's Council of Torah Sages. Peak: 17 seats in 1999.
Deri has led it since 2013 (and 1990–99). Former Chief Rabbi Yitzhak Yosef was chosen “to lead” in 2026.

voters.text: Won 28% of Haredi voters and 10.5% of national-religious voters in 2022.
IDI's Malach: “at least three or four Knesset seats' worth of voters who are simply not Haredi.”
First-time voters: 3% overall, 20% of Haredi first-timers.

draft.text: Deri: “The army doesn't want haredi soldiers, get that into your head.” Bill to enshrine Torah study as a basic value.

courts.text: “Fundamentally reform the judicial system and return power to the people and their elected representatives.”

war.text: Supports dismantling Hamas; opposes indefinite Israeli control (JPost's summary).

wb.text: Opposes a Palestinian state; “not central” to its campaign.

relig.text: Orthodox control of marriage, conversion and kashrut; opposes civil marriage and expanded non-Orthodox prayer at the Kotel.

econ.text: Deri: “It is unacceptable that a poor Haredi child would not receive the minimum support as a poor Arab child does.”

names.name: Lt.-Col. (res.) Dror Amos
names.note: Haifa religious council head; 25 years in the IDF

pledges.text: “We support Netanyahu, period.”
Reported plan to sit in opposition until a draft law passes; anonymous source, “not a formal decision.”

quote.text: Will Bibi Netanyahu repent? Not a chance… Eisenkot, perhaps he will.
quote.speaker: Rabbi Yitzhak Yosef

bios.name: Aryeh Deri
bios.text: Born 1959 in Meknes. Co-founded Shas and became the youngest minister. Convicted of bribery in 1999 and served 22 months; after a 2022 tax plea, the High Court barred him from serving as a minister in January 2023.

who.text: A joint list of Agudat Yisrael (Hasidic) and Degel HaTorah (Lithuanian) since 1992. Both factions quit the government in July 2025 over the draft.
Sept 5, 2026: Rav Dov Landau removed Gafni and Maklev by letter and made Yaakov Asher head. Sept 8: Porush and Stark formed a third faction inside the list, Homat Torat Yisrael, the first since 1992.

voters.text: 58% of Haredim voted UTJ in 2022; 86% voted UTJ or Shas.
2021: 78% in Modi'in Illit, 60.9% in Bnei Brak.
First-time voters: 9% overall, 45% of Haredi first-timers.

draft.text: “United Torah Judaism, with all its components, will not support or enter any government without regulating the status of Torah learners.”

courts.text: “The Supreme Court has accumulated excessive power.”

wb.text: No unified policy; Agudah leans right, Degel “more moderate.”

relig.text: Same as Shas: Orthodox control of marriage, conversion and kashrut.

econ.text: Housing for Haredi communities; yeshiva funding.

pledges.text: No government without a yeshiva-status law, whoever leads it.
Porush's faction requires separate negotiations.
Rav Landau: “We no longer have trust in Netanyahu.”

quote.text: Many things look like etrogim – but this isn't an etrog.
quote.speaker: Yaakov Asher, on Religious Zionism and Otzma courting Haredi voters

bios.name: Yaakov Asher
bios.text: Born July 2, 1965 in Ramat Gan. Mayor of Bnei Brak from 2008; MK since 2013; Deputy Speaker 2022. Resigned as Interior Committee chair over the draft (Ynet, Sep 6, 2026).

bios.name: Yitzhak Goldknopf (no. 2)
bios.text: Born 1950 in Jerusalem; a Ger Hasid who built a kindergarten network. Leader of Agudat Yisrael since 2022. Resigned as housing minister in June 2025 over the draft.

parties.name: Religious Zionism–Zehut
parties.surplusLine: Surplus: Likud (agreed Sep 8; reported unsigned Sep 15)

who.text: From the National Union line; Smotrich has chaired it since 2019. Smotrich refused a new joint run with Ben-Gvir.
On Sept 1, 2026 formed a “technical bloc” with Moshe Feiglin's Zehut that can separate after the election. Feiglin: “We are a totally separate party.”

voters.text: 2022 (joint list with Otzma and Noam): 516,470 votes, 10.84%, 14 seats; RZ kept 7.
The 2022 joint list took 45% of national-religious voters (up from 30%) and 14% of traditional voters.
Won 22% in settlements vs about 11% nationally.
Settler anger over the draft: “I don't have a political home today.”

draft.text: Most RZ MKs voted for the July 14 law banning arrests of draft evaders. Smotrich: arrests “just make Jews fight one another.”
draft.source: Times of Israel, Jul 14 and Aug 7, 2026

courts.text: “These elections concern the judiciary.” Plan: justices chosen by secret ballot of all judges, AG role split in two, 61-vote override.

war.text: “Return to the whole of Gaza in a big way,” with military rule before sovereignty.

wb.text: E1 approval (~3,400 units) “practically erases the two-state delusion.” 103 new settlements approved during his tenure.
wb.source: Times of Israel, Aug 20, 2025; JPost, Aug 18, 2026

relig.text: “Jewish identity in state institutions and education.”

econ.text: “Competition-based solutions”; Zehut adds a flat tax, school vouchers, a professional army and cannabis legalization.

pledges.text: Netanyahu for prime minister; rules out Arab parties.

surplusPartner.text: Likud. Agreed Sept 8; reported still unsigned Sept 15.

quote.text: Every settlement… is another nail in the coffin of this dangerous idea.
quote.speaker: Bezalel Smotrich, on a Palestinian state

bios.name: Bezalel Smotrich
bios.text: Born 1980; lives in Kedumim; co-founded Regavim. Finance minister and a minister in the Defense Ministry over the Civil Administration. Known for a 2023 remark that Huwara should be “wiped out”; sanctioned by several countries since June 2025.

who.text: Amcha Yisrael. Launched Aug 25, 2026 in Jerusalem by Ofer Winter, a retired brigadier general who turned down a Likud slot.
Refused Smotrich's merger offer despite pressure from rabbis. Winter: the public wants “new people.”

voters.text: New list; no 2022 result.
Targets younger voters, reservists, and right-wingers who can't back the current government.
Sector data: not found.

draft.text: “We will not join a government that does not pass, before it is formed, a law that puts an end to draft evasion… Full stop.”

war.text: “There is one solution in Gaza: migration.”

wb.text: “There will never be a Palestinian state here.”

names.name: Yoseph Haddad
names.note: Arab Orthodox Christian; Golani volunteer wounded in 2006

pledges.text: Recommends only Netanyahu; wants the Defense ministry; won't partner with Bennett or Eisenkot (JPost reports conflict).

surplusPartner.text: None. Likud chose Religious Zionism; Ben-Gvir refused.

quote.text: New people, those who were not part of the events that led us to October 7.
quote.speaker: Ofer Winter, on what the public wants

bios.name: Ofer Winter
bios.text: Born Feb 3, 1971 in Rekhasim. In the IDF 1990–2024; commanded Duvdevan, the Givati Brigade and the 98th Division. On Oct 7 he went to the Be'eri front on his own. Retired May 2024 after being passed over for major general. Lives in Mitzpe Netofa.

parties.name: Noam

who.text: Avi Maoz's party. Won 1 seat in 2022 as part of the Religious Zionism joint list; running alone in 2026.
who.source: Wikipedia; CRC research memo Part C

parties.thin: Our research registers have no 2026 profile, polling or bio for Noam or Avi Maoz.

who.text: Founded Sept 16, 2025 by Gadi Eisenkot with about 120 co-founders, after he left the Knesset.
Named for freed hostage Eli Sharabi's line that bringing the captives home was “not about right or left, but straight (yashar).”
2026 recruits include former Shin Bet chief Yoram Cohen, Orit Farkash-Hacohen and Elazar Stern.

voters.text: New list; no 2022 result (Eisenkot ran on National Unity, which won 12 seats).
Targets “Route 4” commuter suburbs: Petah Tikva, Kiryat Ono, Holon; also courting former Likud voters.
voters.source: Times of Israel, Jul 1 and Sep 14, 2026

voters.text: “Security-minded, centrist or moderate-right, secular or religiously traditional.”
Largest share of first-time voters (18–22): 16%.

draft.text: “National Service for All”; deferments capped at 3% of each cohort, about 2,200 people; evaders lose benefits.

courts.text: Repeal the judicial selection law; opposes an override clause; clearer rules for judicial review in a Basic Law.

war.text: “The State of Israel must not accept a reality in which Hamas survives, rearms, and waits.” Wants a state commission of inquiry.

wb.text: Opposes a Palestinian state; would put the Civil Administration back under military coordination.

relig.text: “A secular party, but not anti-religious”; supports civil and same-sex marriage (JC's summary).

econ.text: 15% raise for all conscripts; renter protections; reserve duty capped at 50 days a year.

pledges.text: Partners must accept four principles, including service for all and Hamas “to be dismantled and destroyed.” “I do not rule out any Zionist party.”
On Ra'am: Mansour Abbas “won't be part of my next government.” No Haredi party currently meets his criteria.

quote.text: Netanyahu initially opposed including that objective, and I forced it upon him on the ninth day of the war.
quote.speaker: Gadi Eisenkot, on making the hostages a war goal

bios.name: Gadi Eisenkot
bios.text: Born 1960 in Tiberias to immigrants from Morocco. Commanded the Golani Brigade and Northern Command; IDF Chief of Staff 2015–19. His son Gal was killed in Gaza in December 2023, at 25. JTA: he would be Israel's first Mizrahi prime minister.

who.text: “Together – Led by Bennett.” Yesh Atid runs inside this list under a deal signed Apr 25–26, 2026; Lapid is no. 2 and Yesh Atid holds 10 of the top 24 slots. Not a formal merger.
Polling fell from about 25 seats in May to roughly half; the list has tacked toward the liberal-Zionist center.

voters.text: 2022: Yesh Atid 847,435 votes, 17.79%, 24 seats; Bennett did not run.
Yesh Atid's 2022 voters were 78.5% secular, 20% traditional; it took 39% of the secular vote.
Russian speakers: Bennett 17%.
First-time voters: 10%.

draft.text: Bennett: “Bibi is talking about a 50% exemption, Gadi is talking about a 30% exemption, I am talking about 0 exemption.” End stipends for married yeshiva students.

courts.text: A Basic Law on how Basic Laws are made and when courts may step in; repeal the judicial appointments law; 8-year term limits for prime ministers.

war.text: “We must not budge a centimeter from the red line until Hamas is disarmed.” Supports a state commission on Oct 7.

wb.text: Opposes a Palestinian state “under any constellation”; backs E1; would dismantle illegal outposts while backing “legal settlement in Area C.”
wb.source: JPost, Aug 30; Times of Israel, Jun 23, 2026

relig.text: Civil marriage; cities choose on Shabbat transit; “full equality of rights to protect the LGBTQ community.”

econ.text: “We will cut food prices by 30% within three years.”

pledges.text: Zionist parties only: no Arab or Haredi parties; “no compromises on draft issues.”
An explicit break from his 2021 government with Ra'am.

quote.text: I'm a right-wing guy, I'm not changing my opinions. But I'm not a schmuck.
quote.speaker: Naftali Bennett

bios.name: Naftali Bennett
bios.text: Born 1972 in Haifa to American parents. Served in Sayeret Matkal, built tech companies (Cyota, Soluto), and led the Yesha Council 2010–12. Prime minister June 2021–June 2022, the first to wear a kippah.

bios.name: Yair Lapid (no. 2)
bios.text: Born 1963; a former TV host who founded Yesh Atid in 2012 (19 seats in 2013). Prime minister July–December 2022, then opposition leader.

parties.name: The Democrats

who.text: Labor (founded 1968; prime ministers Meir, Rabin, Peres) and Meretz (1992) running together. A partial merger: both keep their own institutions.
Yair Golan won Labor's leadership in May 2024 with 95%. Protest leaders joined in 2026, including Moshe Radman and Gaby Lasky.

voters.text: 2022: Labor 175,992 votes, 3.69%, 4 seats; Meretz 150,793, 3.16%, 0 seats (its first time out of the Knesset).
Labor and Meretz took 16% of the secular vote in 2022, down from 19%.
First-time voters: 7%. Claims more than 100,000 members.

draft.text: Universal service “within a national and equal framework.” Golan has called mass Haredi conscription “impractical.”
draft.source: Ynet, Sep 16; Times of Israel, Aug 5, 2026

courts.text: Urgent problems are “delays, overloaded courts and a shortage of judges”; an intermediate appeals court; opposes the 2023 reform.

wb.text: Opposes annexation; defund outposts. Golan: civil separation with Israeli security control.

relig.text: Civil marriage; limited Shabbat public transport in secular towns; amend the Nation-State Law.

econ.text: “Reduce living costs, improve social services, rebuild the public sector”; JPost calls the detail “less clearly defined.”

parties.namesSource: June 20 primary results, CRC party register

pledges.text: No Likud, no Haredi parties.
Open to an Arab party: “It is natural, right, appropriate and democratic” (the party says this is its own platform, not the bloc's).
pledges.source: Kan via Times of Israel, Sep 27, 2026

quote.text: In our government, there will be zero criminal defendants. Zero.
quote.speaker: Yair Golan

bios.name: Yair Golan
bios.text: Born 1962. A former IDF deputy chief of staff, known for a 2016 Holocaust Remembrance Day speech. On October 7 he rescued Nova festival survivors; elected Labor leader in May 2024 with 95%.

parties.name: Yisrael Beiteinu

who.text: Founded 1999 by Avigdor Lieberman; first aimed at Soviet immigrants, later “right-wing secular voters.” Peak: 15 seats in 2009.
His April 2019 refusal to join a government over the draft law set off five elections.

voters.text: Russian speakers: Yisrael Beiteinu 23%; 94% of them back a universal draft.
First-time voters: 6%.

draft.text: Everyone at 18: “Jews, Muslims, Christians, Druze and Circassians”; sanctions including travel bans.

courts.text: A written constitution put to a national referendum; amendments would need 80 MKs.

war.text: Board of Peace arrangements are “a capitulation to terror.” A state commission on Oct 7 is a condition.
war.source: JPost, Aug 12; Times of Israel, Aug 17, 2026

relig.text: Civil marriage and divorce; a Western Wall compromise; local choice on Shabbat transit; a mandatory core curriculum.

names.name: Sharon Sharabi
names.note: brother of freed hostage Eli Sharabi

parties.namesSource: JPost and Times of Israel, Sep 6, 2026

pledges.text: No Netanyahu, no Arab parties, no Haredi parties: “not for the Arab parties and not for the haredi parties.”
Conditions: Oct 7 inquiry, universal service, prime-minister term limits, core curriculum, constitution by referendum.

quote.text: We are the Likud of yesteryear.
quote.speaker: Yisrael Beiteinu slogan

bios.name: Avigdor Lieberman
bios.text: Born 1958 in Chișinău; immigrated in 1978 and lives in Nokdim. Founded Yisrael Beiteinu in 1999. His refusal to join a government in April 2019 started the cycle of five elections.

parties.name: Blue and White
parties.status: Below threshold in every recent poll

who.text: Down to 3 MKs after defections. Gantz will drop out in the last week if the party is not crossing the threshold.

parties.thin: Our party registers do not profile Blue and White beyond this.

bios.name: Benny Gantz
bios.text: Born 1959 to Holocaust survivors. IDF Chief of Staff 2011–15. His Blue and White tied Likud three times in 2019–20; alternate prime minister in 2020. Left the war cabinet June 9, 2024.

who.text: Yoaz Hendel founded The Reservists on Sept 18, 2025. It runs as a technical joint list with Yaron Zelekha's New Economic Party (filed Sept 7, 2026).
Pitches itself as a “third bloc.” Its bloc is disputed: IsraelEd says it would join Netanyahu; Times of Israel calls it non-aligned.

voters.text: New list; no 2022 seats. Zelekha's party won 0.29% (13,920 votes) in 2022.

Hendel: “Those wanting government with ultra-Orthodox parties know who to vote for… Those comfortable with minority government relying on Arab parties have their opposition choice. We must provide the alternative.”
First crossed the threshold in Channel 13's Sept 23 poll. Sector data: not found.

draft.text: “Those who do not serve cannot vote or be elected to the Knesset.” A draft law must pass before a government is sworn in.

courts.text: Reform, 8-year term limits, a constitution and a “Basic Law: Legislation.”

war.text: Hendel earlier proposed moving about 1.5 million Gazans to “a tent city outside the Strip”; Wilf backs a “voluntary emigration directorate for Gaza.”

wb.text: “We will not allow a Palestinian state to be established… we support settlement.”

econ.text: Zelekha: Israel is “a paradise for monopolies”; an apartment costs about 170 average salaries.

pledges.text: Zionist government only (no Haredi or Arab parties); universal-draft law; state commission; a national security ministry for Hendel.
On Netanyahu, mixed: “Netanyahu is not my red line” (Aug 11) vs. “whoever is responsible for October 7 needs to go home, and that includes Netanyahu” (Aug 23).

surplusPartner.text: None confirmed. IPF lists Yisrael Beiteinu, but Yisrael Beiteinu signed with B'Yachad.

quote.text: Our mission is solely to establish a Zionist government.
quote.speaker: The Reservists

bios.name: Yoaz Hendel
bios.text: Born 1975 in Petah Tikva, raised in Elkana. Shayetet 13; a reserve lieutenant-colonel who commanded Battalion 8555 in the 2023 war. Netanyahu's communications director 2011–12; communications minister in 2020 and 2021–22.

who.text: First formed in 2015 by all four Arab-led parties (13 seats; peak of 15 in 2020). Re-formed Aug 19, 2026 as Hadash–Ta'al–Balad, without Ra'am.
The Central Elections Committee voted Sept 23 to bar it, 18–5. The Supreme Court heard the appeal Oct 1 and reinstated it 9–0 on Oct 2. No. 3 Sami Abu Shehadeh withdrew.
who.source: Times of Israel, Sep 23; JPost, Oct 2, 2026

voters.text: 2022 (ran split): Hadash–Ta'al 178,735 votes, 3.75%, 5 seats; Balad 138,617, 2.91%, 0 seats.
In Arab and Druze towns in 2022: Hadash–Ta'al 28.8%, Balad 21.7%. Arab turnout 53.2%.
77.2% of Arab citizens support an Arab party joining the government.

war.text: “End Gaza destruction and West Bank ethnic cleansing.”

wb.text: Jabareen: renewed negotiations toward “a Palestinian state alongside Israel.”

relig.text: “Full civic and national equality for Arab citizens.”

pledges.text: Won't join Netanyahu.
Conditions for backing an Eisenkot bloc: equality, a development plan, real action on crime, “a clear position against settlements”; did not rule out “a parliamentary safety net.”

quote.text: A political, racist, and anti-democratic decision… an attempt to exclude the political representation of more than one million voters.
quote.speaker: The Joint List, on the committee's vote to bar it

bios.name: Yousef Jabareen
bios.text: Born 1972 in Umm al-Fahm. A constitutional-law scholar with a Georgetown PhD; MK 2015–21. Elected Hadash chair May 16, 2026 with 82%, replacing Ayman Odeh, who is not on the 2026 ballot.

bios.name: Ahmad Tibi (no. 2)
bios.text: Born 1958 in Tayibe; a gynecologist. Adviser to Arafat 1993–99; MK since 1999.

who.text: Founded 1996 as the political wing of the Islamic Movement's Southern Branch. In 2021 it became the first independent Arab party in an Israeli government.
Opened membership to all Israelis in Jan 2026 and declared its split from the Shura Council complete in July 2026.
Barred by the Elections Committee Sept 23; reinstated 9–0 by the Supreme Court Oct 2.
who.source: Times of Israel, Sep 23; JPost, Oct 2, 2026

voters.text: Took 35.2% of the Arab and Druze vote in 2022, and 73.9% in the Negev.
Strongholds: the Negev and the Triangle; now seeking Christian and Druze voters, with a 7–8 seat target.

war.text: Asked whether Hamas is a terror group to be destroyed: “I have a straight answer; I just don't want to say it.”

wb.text: “The state of Palestine exists and stands… We want them to recognize it too.”

relig.text: Earlier: “Israel was born as a Jewish state, and it will remain so.” The AG told the committee Abbas recognizes Israel's Jewish character.

econ.text: Budgets, planning, housing and jobs for Arab towns; seeks the violence and crime portfolio. No full manifesto.

names.name: Yoav Segalovitz
names.note: Jewish former police commander; joined Aug 31

names.name: Walid Taha
names.note: on the Aug 22 slate; final slot not confirmed

pledges.text: Open to any coalition, including one led by Likud.
Eisenkot said Sept 26 that Abbas “won't be part of my next government.” Segalovitz: “Eisenkot won't have a government without Ra'am.”

quote.text: I am going to an Arab party. They are not coming to me.
quote.speaker: Yoav Segalovitz
quote.source: as quoted in CRC party register, Oct 4, 2026

bios.name: Mansour Abbas
bios.text: Born 1974 in Maghar; a dentist and imam. Describes himself as “an Arab, a Palestinian, a Muslim, and a citizen of the State of Israel.” Ra'am chair since 2018.

bios.name: Yoav Segalovitz (no. 2)
bios.text: Jewish, 67. Former commander of Lahav 433 and head of the police Investigations Division; former deputy public security minister. Joins Ra'am's Knesset faction, not the party (JPost; Times of Israel, Aug 31, 2026).
